newsitem.title: USA: Nationwide Financial surges after IPO.
newsitem.headline: Nationwide Financial surges after IPO.

text.p: Nationwide Financial's stock surged nearly 15 percent Thursday as the nation's fifth-largest property-casualty insurer was spun off by Nationwide Insurance Enterprise in a $480 million initial public offering.
The stock rose $3.375 to $26.875 on the New York Stock Exchange, where it was the most active issue with 11.3 million shares changing hands.
The rally had been expected as the offering was oversubscribed by 12 times, an analyst said.
About 20.5 million shares were priced at $23.50, above initial estimates of $21 to $23. That range was raised to $23 to $24 a share by lead underwriter Credit Suisse First Boston.
Nationwide Insurance spun off part of the company to fund the expansion of its fast-growing life insurance business.
At least 80 percent of Nationwide Financial's outstanding shares will be owned by a member of the Nationwide Insurance group of companies, it said.
As a mutual insurance company, Nationwide Insurance is owned by its policyholders and therefore does not have access to the public equity markets.
